question: If the side of a square is measured 4% more than its actual length, what is the percentage error in the area of the square?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Area depends on square of side

Error = 2x + x²

Here x = 4%

Error = 2(4) + (4)²/100 = 8 + 0.16

**∴ Answer = 8.16%**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Side is measured 4% more

**Formula used:**

Area of square = side²

**Calculation:**

⇒ Let actual side = 100 units

⇒ Measured side = 104 units

⇒ Actual area = 100 × 100 = 10000

⇒ Measured area = 104 × 104 = 10816

⇒ Error in area = 10816 − 10000 = 816

⇒ Percentage error = (816 ÷ 10000) × 100

⇒ = 8.16%

**∴ The correct answer is 8.16%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Error Formula

If side error = x%, area error ≈ 2x + x²/100

Square Relation

Area ∝ (side)²

Approximation Tip

For small errors, 2x is dominant term

Exact Method

Use actual values to avoid approximation errors
